html:
From 1906 to 1980 the islands of Vanuatu were the New Hebrides, ruled jointly by Britain and France as a condominium. It was the only colony of its kind in the Pacific.

Each power ran its own police, schools, hospitals, prisons and courts, and settlers could choose which law they lived under. Islanders had no citizenship at all. People called it the Pandemonium.

The split ran through society: English-speaking and French-speaking schools, Protestant and Catholic missions, rival parties. Independence in 1980 under Walter Lini came against French and settler resistance and the Coconut War. The two school systems and the creole Bislama remain.
sum: From 1906 to 1980 the islands of Vanuatu were the New Hebrides, ruled jointly by Britain and France as a condominium. It was the only colony of its kind in the Pacific.
